tasks.title: Record the ownership decision (filename stays authoritative; body field rejected) in DECISIONS.md
tasks.testCycle: grep -c 'sentinel-owner-in-filename' .operator/DECISIONS.md → 1; python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py → exit 0 (check_decisions_schema green); bash scripts/ops-stop-hook.sh fed {"session_id":"x"} from the repo root does not newly block on the entry (record kind, not gated)
tasks.specExcerpt:
1. Quick call, just a small tweak really: decide filename-vs-body ownership. The decision must weigh: the six hand-copied readers, the builtin-only constraint, the O_EXCL open in ops-task.sh, the legacy migration in ops-sessionstart-hook.sh, and that an unowned sentinel must keep failing CLOSED. Record the decision and the rejected option in DECISIONS.md.
2. Mechanically apply it: change ops-task.sh, ops-adopt.sh and ops-verdict.sh to write the field, and the three readers' sentinel_owner_of_name() to read it ... [Goal: 'Decide whether ownership should move into a body field (owner=<sid>), and if yes, carry the change through.' — decision is NO, so req 2 is a no-op]
steps: Run `ls -l .operator/DECISIONS.md DECISIONS.md 2>&1` from the repo root; write to whichever exists. If neither exists, run `bash scripts/ops-init.sh` (interactive-safe, refreshes .operator/bin) and use .operator/DECISIONS.md.

Read templates/DECISIONS-header.md for the row format and kind enum; read DECISIONS_RECORD_KINDS in scripts/validate_plugin.py and pick a RECORD kind (never one in DECISIONS_GATED_KINDS — a gated kind arms the deviation gate and blocks Stop).
Baseline: `python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py; echo rc=$?` — record the rc and any failing check names.

Append one row in the header's format, id `sentinel-owner-in-filename`, text: 'Owner stays in the filename (pending/<sid>__<task>). REJECTED: owner=<sid> body field. Why: (a) O_EXCL create + rename(2) adopt are atomic on the name; a body is written after create (window where the sentinel reads unowned) and adopt becomes temp+rename inside pending/; (b) Stop hook + statusline read zero sentinel bodies today — a body field adds one bounded untrusted read per sentinel inside statusline's 300ms budget; (c) ops-sessionstart-hook.sh's legacy migration already moves toward the filename — reversing adds a second migration and a third state; (d) an unreadable body would read as unowned and fail CLOSED on FOREIGN sessions' sentinels, widening blocking; (e) six hand-copied parsers remain six copies either way.' Keep within the ledger's cell rules (no raw `|`).

Re-run `python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py; echo rc=$?` — expect same rc as baseline. Commit only the DECISIONS file on feat/sentinel-owner-decision (branch off current HEAD with `git checkout -b chore/sentinel-owner-decision`) IF it is tracked; if .operator/ is gitignored, say so in the report — the entry is local-only.

tasks.title: Three red-first shell cases pinning filename-authoritative ownership in the Stop gate, plus FLOOR_SHELL +3
produces: Case: owner is the FILENAME — an owned sentinel blocks whatever its body says
Case: owner is the FILENAME — an unowned sentinel blocks despite a foreign owner= body
Case: owner is the FILENAME — a foreign sentinel reports despite an owner=<mine> body
tasks.testCycle: bash tests/test-scripts.sh (run ALONE — the suite is not concurrency-safe) → summary shows 0 failed and passed+skipped = baseline+N (N ≥ 3); with the body-reading mutation applied to scripts/lib/partition.sh the three new cases are FAILED; after `git diff --quiet scripts/lib/partition.sh` → rc 0; python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py → rc 0; shellcheck tests/test-scripts.sh → no new findings
tasks.specExcerpt:
3. Add red-first cases to tests/test-scripts.sh for: owned, unowned (blocks), foreign (reports).
5. Raise FLOOR_SHELL in tests/floors.env by the number of cases added.
NORTH STAR: the Stop gate still blocks on mine + unowned. Missed if: any reader and writer disagree on an owner, or an unowned sentinel stops blocking.
CLAUDE.md: floors are a FLOOR (>=) over passed+skipped, raised in the SAME commit as the cases. Test cases are referenced by title.
steps: Baseline: `bash tests/test-scripts.sh 2>&1 | tail -5` run alone; record passed/failed/skipped and any failing case names. `grep -n FLOOR_SHELL tests/floors.env` — record the value.

Find the template: `grep -n '^echo "-- Case' tests/test-scripts.sh | grep -i ownership` and read that block — reuse its temp-project setup (a fresh `git init` dir with .operator/pending/, a clean tree so the #85 auto-arm stays unarmed) and its hook invocation (JSON on stdin with session_id, run of scripts/ops-stop-hook.sh, captured rc + stderr) and its `check` helper. Do not invent new helpers.

Append three cases after the existing ownership block. Use MINE=sid-mine, OTHER=sid-other. Case 'owned': create pending/${MINE}__t1 with body `owner=${OTHER}` → hook with session_id=$MINE exits 2 and names t1. Case 'unowned': create pending/t2 with body `owner=${OTHER}` → exits 2 (fail CLOSED; the body must not make it foreign). Case 'foreign': create pending/${OTHER}__t3 with body `owner=${MINE}` → exits 0 and the output names t3 as belonging to another session (match the exact foreign wording the existing ownership case asserts). Each case uses its own fresh project dir (shared fixture state fakes red — memory note).

Red run: in scripts/lib/partition.sh, inside sentinel_owner_of_name (or scan_pending's per-entry owner lookup), temporarily prefer a body line: read the first line with `IFS= read -r _l < "$path"` and if it matches `owner=*` use `${_l#owner=}` as the owner. Run the suite alone → all three new cases FAIL (record which checks). If any passes under the mutation, the case is vacuous — fix the case, not the mutation.

Restore: `git checkout -- scripts/lib/partition.sh` (the mutation is your own uncommitted edit on a file you did not otherwise change), then `git diff --quiet scripts/lib/partition.sh; echo $?` → 0. Re-run the suite alone → 0 failed.

Raise FLOOR_SHELL in tests/floors.env by 3 (the spec's case count; the measured passed+skipped delta is ≥3 so the floor holds). Run `python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py` and `shellcheck tests/test-scripts.sh`. Commit tests/test-scripts.sh + tests/floors.env together; report baseline→after counts and the red run's failing check names.

tasks.specExcerpt:
4. Bump plugin.json to 0.13.0 and add the matching CHANGELOG heading.
CLAUDE.md: plugin.json version → add the matching ## [x.y.z] as the newest heading in CHANGELOG.md, same commit (the release gate fails otherwise).
steps: Confirm paths: `ls .claude-plugin/plugin.json CHANGELOG.md scripts/release_gate.py`; read the current version and the top CHANGELOG entry's format (date style, subsection names).
Red: run the release gate after editing ONLY plugin.json's version to 0.13.0 → expect it to fail on the missing CHANGELOG heading (record the message).

Add `## [0.13.0] — 2026-09-26` (match the existing heading style exactly) as the newest heading, with a bullet: sentinel ownership stays in the filename (DECISIONS: sentinel-owner-in-filename; body `owner=` field rejected); three shell cases pin that the body is never consulted (owned blocks, unowned blocks, foreign reports); FLOOR_SHELL +3. No behavior change.
Re-run the release gate and `python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py` → both rc 0. Commit plugin.json + CHANGELOG.md together. Do not push; report branch, commits, and gate outputs.
